title: Facing the House
hookLine: wherever you are, you face the Ka'ba in Mecca

lines: AN ARROW IN A HOTEL ROOM.
cards: A hotel room in Istanbul. On the ceiling above the bed, or on a little sticker by the desk, there's an arrow. It isn't pointing to the exit.
In Chicago, someone opens a prayer app, and a compass needle swings and settles. In a mosque, there's a niche in one wall, the mihrab, and every line of people stands facing it.
Starting points all over the earth, all turning toward one small building in one valley.

teach.b: The word is qiblah, the direction a person faces in prayer, from a root meaning to face, to be in front of.
The qiblah is the Ka'ba, the cube-shaped House in Mecca that the Qur'an says Ibrahim and Isma'il raised. But it wasn't always.
A hadith in Bukhari says that after the move to Medina, for sixteen or seventeen months, the Muslims prayed facing Jerusalem.

Then, the Qur'an says in Surah al-Baqarah, the Prophet ﷺ kept turning his face toward the sky, and the verse came: turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.
The hadith collections tell what happened next. A man who had prayed with the Prophet passed a mosque where people were mid-prayer, still facing Jerusalem, and told them.

teach.h: THEY TURNED IN THE MIDDLE OF PRAYER.
teach.b: They turned around, right there in the prayer, to face Mecca. A mosque in Medina is still called the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs.
Underneath is an idea from earlier in the same surah: the East and the West belong to Allah, and wherever you turn, there is His face. So Muslims don't say God lives in the Ka'ba.
The direction isn't about where God is. It's about where the people are pointed, so a worshipper in Jakarta and one in Lagos stand in the same line. One honest wrinkle.
From North America, people work out the direction two ways. Along the shortest path over the curve of the globe, Mecca is to the northeast. Along a straight line on a flat map, it's to the southeast.
Communities have followed each, and both are trying to face the same House.

how: Muslims face the Ka'ba in Mecca for every prayer; mosques mark the direction with a niche called the mihrab, and many people use a compass or a phone app when they pray away from home.

o: the journey Muslims make on pilgrimage to Mecca
the direction Muslims face to pray, toward Mecca
the niche in a mosque wall that holds the Qur'an

games.q: what's inside the qiblah — tap the pairs.
p: the direction you face in prayer
the niche that marks the direction

s: Muslims face Mecca because they believe God lives in the Ka'ba
the Qur'an says wherever you turn, there is the face of Allah. the direction unites the people.
the earliest Muslims prayed facing Jerusalem
until the verse came in Medina telling them to turn toward the Sacred Mosque.
from North America, everyone faces southeast
communities differ: some face northeast, the shortest path on a round earth; some face southeast, a straight line on a map.

games.q: you're in the middle of a prayer, facing Jerusalem. a man walks in and says the qiblah has changed to Mecca. what do you do?
o: finish facing Jerusalem, and change next time
stop and start the prayer over
games.why: the hadith says they turned around in the middle of the prayer to face Mecca. a mosque in Medina is still called the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs.

practice: Find the qiblah from where you are, with a compass or a phone app, or roughly: Mecca is in western Arabia, so from Europe it's southeast, from India west, and from North America northeast or southeast, depending on the method your community follows.
Turn your body that way and sit still for a moment, picturing the lines of people all over the earth facing the same point you are. If you pray, this is where you'd face.

wordCard.voice: Qiblah. The direction of prayer, toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, turned from Jerusalem in the Prophet's time. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the direction faced in prayer, from a root meaning to face, to be in front of.

carryVoice: Your line: all turned one way. Starting points all over the earth, and one House. Day ninety-nine, done.

sources.ref: Qur'an 2:144 (turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque)
Qur'an 2:115 (the East and the West belong to Allah; wherever you turn, there is His face)
Qur'an 2:127 (Ibrahim and Isma'il raising the foundations of the House)
Sahih al-Bukhari 40 and 403 (the change of qiblah; people turning mid-prayer)
